svg.title: The tile-list cut: render a target through only the tiles it covers
svg.desc: The PVR renders tile by tile, 32 by 32 pixels. A render target rendered through the screen's whole tile list walks all 300 tiles of a 640 by 480 screen. Cut to the tiles the target covers, the 128 by 128 map pass fell from 3,312 to 375 microseconds (20 tiles) and the 320 by 240 mask pass from 6,130 to 3,760 microseconds (80 tiles), with the same picture. One console, 2026-11-25.
svg.text: The tile-list cut: render a target through only the tiles it covers
The PVR renders one 32 x 32 tile at a time; the depth buffer lives on chip per tile [FACT Sega §3.4.4, PVR-083]. Each square below is a tile of the 640 x 480 screen.
Green: tiles the target covers. Beige: tiles the pass walks although nothing of the target is in them.
Map pass: 128 x 130 target (4 x 5 = 20 tiles)

1,806 = 6 + 300 x 6 words: one entry a screen tile [ESTIMATE].
A target pass's 3.2 ms floor is likely this walk [ESTIMATE PVR-004].
